headline: CESC Limited: Disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations by Rainbow Investments Limited
sum: Rainbow Investments Limited has filed a SEBI Regulation 31(4) disclosure with NSE regarding a substantial acquisition of shares in CESC Limited. The filing constitutes a mandatory disclosure under the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, signaling a triggering event in shareholding.
implication: Regulation 31(4) disclosure is a precursor to either a public open offer or a negotiated settlement; the acquirer's next step will depend on the quantum of shares acquired and whether 25% or 50%+ threshold has been crossed, determining open offer vs. exemption eligibility under the Takeover Code.
detail: Rainbow Investments Limited has submitted a formal disclosure to NSE under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI Takeover Regulations 2011, concerning a substantial acquisition in CESC Limited (a Kolkata-based integrated power utility). The disclosure triggers mandatory public announcement and transparency requirements. The actual shareholding percentage, consideration amount, and offer terms are documented in the filed disclosure form, which is archived in NSE's corporate action portal. This is a regulated capital markets event requiring clearance-of-title verification and minority shareholder protection mechanisms under Indian law.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011
framework.note: Regulation 31(4) mandates disclosure when 25% or more shares are acquired; regulates public offers, exemptions, and tender mechanics.
Defines 'promoter', 'acquirer' and triggering acquisition thresholds (25%, 50%); governs applicability of Code.
Prescribes public announcement requirements, timing, and content of disclosure for substantial acquisitions.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
framework.note: Grants SEBI authority to regulate takeovers and substantial acquisitions to protect investor interests.
Requires registration of charges and substantial shareholding changes; complements takeover code filings.

framework.ref: NSE Listing Rules and Regulation of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
framework.note: Mandates listed companies to maintain disclosure of shareholding and significant corporate actions via exchange filings.

framework.ref: Prevention of Unfair Manipulation of Securities Markets (PUMAM) Rules, 2023
framework.note: Anti-fraud overlay ensuring disclosed information is accurate and no market manipulation occurs around substantial acquisitions.

framework.ref: IEPF (Investor Education and Protection Fund) Act, 2023 (to extent applicable to shareholder communications)
framework.note: Governs shareholder approval and communications in public offer scenarios.

conditions: Filing of SEBI Regulation 31(4) disclosure with NSE
Public announcement of acquisition (likely required unless exemption sought)
Compliance with takeover code tender mechanics (if open offer triggered)
approvals: SEBI clearance / deemed acceptance of disclosure
CCI approval (if combined acquisition crosses ₹2,000 cr turnover threshold)
RBI approval (if acquirer or target is banking/financial entity)
structure.novel: Regulation 31(4) represents a mandatory regulatory checkpoint for all substantial acquisitions in India; the disclosure is a *condition precedent* to any public offer, private arrangement or exemption plea. No consideration or mechanics can proceed prior to this filing.

triggers.law: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011
triggers.note: Filing triggered upon acquisition of 25% or more shares; mandatory within 2 trading days of crossing threshold.
CCI approval may be required if combined turnover exceeds ₹2,000 cr, though utility acquisitions often scrutinized under Section 5(a)(e) for market concentration.
If Rainbow Investments is foreign-controlled, FEMA filings and RBI/FIPB approvals required.
Company must immediately disclose the acquisition to stock exchange and shareholders.
